key_insight: SCRINN builds an approximately orthonormal neural basis with sparse connections, then solves output weights by least squares to improve efficiency in function approximation and PDE solving.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces trainable parameters and training cost, making neural PDE solvers more practical for large-scale optimization and simulation workflows.
method: Use a sparsely connected architecture to grow rank progressively while keeping parameters low.
Add orthogonality- and normalization-guided losses to shape an approximately orthonormal basis.
Train in two stages: learn the basis first, then compute output weights with least squares.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on function approximation and multiple steady-state, time-dependent, and nonlinear PDEs, showing high accuracy with substantially lower training costs.
watch_item: The two-stage approach and orthogonality constraints may add implementation complexity and could be sensitive to hyperparameter choices or basis construction quality.
